rubric_items.reason: Each of AC1-AC5 and the user story maps to REQ-1..REQ-13. The patient chooser and the dashboard tile are listed under Out of scope with reasons.
Most REQs are atomic and can be tested. REQ-2 bundles two behaviours: the chooser is always shown, and the chooser can clear the doctor filter.
Every known REQ cites a ticket line or an IDE answer, and nothing is invented. One claim (C5) adds an inference that its source does not contain, but no REQ depends on it.
The clash between Inactive in the glossary and the chooser contents was raised as Q-01 with the glossary quoted, and the user answered it. No clash with the baseline was missed.
Q-01..Q-04 were precise, offered real options and went to an engineer. None of them could have been answered from the context pack.
The wording is plain, and glossary terms (Front-desk staff, Cancelled, Inactive) are used consistently.
